subject: Architecture
title: Pruitt-Igoe: The Housing Project That Failed
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pruitt-Igoe: The Housing Project That Failed.

hook.text: Pruitt-Igoe was a 33-building housing project in St. Louis — demolished just 20 years after it was built.

buildup.text: Designed by Minoru Yamasaki — who later designed the World Trade Center — it housed 2,870 apartments.

discovery.text: Budget cuts killed landscaping, playgrounds, and bathrooms. Elevators stopped on every third floor.

twist.text: Crime, vandalism, and vacancy rates soared. The buildings became uninhabitable within a decade.

climax.text: The 1972 demolition was broadcast on TV. Architect Charles Jencks called it 'the death of modernism.'

punchline.text: Good architecture without good funding is just expensive failure.

quiz.question: Why did Pruitt-Igoe fail as a housing project?
options: An earthquake damaged the building foundations beyond repair
Budget cuts removed essential amenities and maintenance funding
The location was contaminated with industrial waste

details.summary: Pruitt-Igoe was a 33-building social housing complex in St. Louis, designed by Minoru Yamasaki and opened in 1954. Within two decades, crime, poverty, and neglect made it unlivable. Its dramatic demolition in 1972 became a symbol of modernist urban planning's failure.
details.whyItMatters: Pruitt-Igoe showed that architecture alone cannot solve social problems. Without adequate funding, maintenance, and community support, even well-designed buildings can become traps rather than homes.
takeaways: Pruitt-Igoe was a 33-building St. Louis housing project from 1954
Crime, poverty, and neglect made it uninhabitable within 20 years
Its demolition symbolized the failure of modernist housing

faq.question: Why did Pruitt-Igoe fail?
faq.answer: Multiple factors combined: underfunded maintenance, racial segregation policies, white flight that eroded the tax base, skip-stop elevator design that created unsafe corridors, and the absence of community spaces. The architecture was a symptom, not the cause, of systemic failures.

faq.question: Who designed Pruitt-Igoe?
faq.answer: Minoru Yamasaki, who later designed the World Trade Center. His original Pruitt-Igoe plans included community spaces and landscaping that were cut to save money. The built version was a stripped-down shadow of the design, fatally compromised before a single resident moved in.
